title: Deployment regression sleuth and safeguard automation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: After a recent canary rollout that produced intermittent semantic regressions and latency spikes, we need a focused ticket to build a lightweight 'Regression Sleuth' toolkit plus automated safeguards that (1) surface root-cause signals quickly, (2) quarantine affected traffic slices automatically, and (3) drive fast postmortem actionability. Background: The failed rollout in Feb exposed gaps: noisy signal aggregation across models/routes, late detection of small but customer-visible output degradation, and manual rollback processes that were slow and error-prone. Current runbooks require human confirmation on multiple dashboards before abort; that increases time-to-rollback and blast radius. Goals: - Automate detection of degradation classes we saw in the incident (generation coherence drop, elevated hallucination rate on prompt set A, 99th latency regressions) - Provide deterministic quarantine rules tied to traffic attributes (region, customer tier, model variant) - Wire an auto-quarantine + notify flow that temporarily redirects affected traffic to previous stable variant and creates a postmortem stub ticket - Produce a compact sleuth UI in Console to iterate on signals and validate quarantine heuristics - Maintain guardrails: human-in-the-loop for broader rollouts, and kill-switch to disable auto actions Requirements & Acceptance criteria: 1) Detection: implement streaming anomaly detector that consumes canary telemetry (latency histograms, eval-based quality scorables, token-level error spikes) and raises a standardized event within 30s of sustained deviation. 2) Quarantine: a policy engine that can route 100% of traffic from an identified slice to fallback variant within 60s and record the decision in audit logs. 3) Automation: a configurable auto-quarantine toggle per project with sensible defaults (thresholds, cool-down windows) and a generated postmortem template including links to top failing prompts, sample outputs, and affected customer IDs. 4) Observability: dashboards and alert runbooks auto-populated from the detection event with links to perf traces, kv-cache metrics, and PRs. 5) Safety: require two independent signals (one quality and one infra) for automated quarantine by default; allow single-signal quarantine under a high-strictness testing mode only. Design trade-offs considered: - Strict automation reduces time-to-mitigate but risks false positives (incorrectly quarantining innocuous traffic). We mitigate via two-signal default and a temporary circuit breaker. - Heavyweight eval runs per-request are too expensive; we rely on sampled evals and synthetic prompt probes during canary windows. - Full automation for enterprises is acceptable only under opt-in because of customer trust and compliance needs. Implementation plan (phases): Phase 1 (1 week, PoC): - Build lightweight detector ingesting existing canary metrics stream and a sampled evaluation runner (10 qps) - Prototype quarantine action that flips traffic routing for a single route in test cluster Phase 2 (2 weeks): - Harden detector thresholds using last 6 weeks of historical baseline data - Add two-signal gating logic and audit log events - Implement auto-postmortem template generation and ticket creation integration with Linear/Confluence Phase 3 (2 weeks): - Console UI for sleuthing events and toggling auto-quarantine per project - Integration tests, chaos simulations, and runbook updates to include the auto-flow Rollout & testing: - Start in shadow mode (no action) for one week on internal beta routes and compare decisions to manual triage - Enable auto-quarantine on non-customer-facing test tenants with canary traffic only - Gradual enablement: internal -> early-access customers (opt-in) -> all canaries (opt-out) Telemetry & signals we will use: - Latency p50/p95/p99 histograms, tail latencies per shard - Eval-based quality score over seeded prompt set (daily and sampled realtime probes) - Output divergence metric vs baseline (BLEU-like for structured outputs, semantic similarity for free text) - KV-cache hit/miss rates, batch sizes, GPU util, kernel fallbacks Risks & mitigation: - False positives: two-signal gate, conservative default thresholds, human confirmation window for high-impact slices - Observability gaps: ensure synthetic probes cover edge prompts, and tag customer queries in canary for retrospective analysis - Compliance: ensure audit log entries contain non-sensitive identifiers only and KMS keys are used for any secret material Documentation & runbooks to deliver: - Runbook: 'Canary Regression Sleuth — Incident flow' (Confluence link in links) - Playbook update: auto-quarantine kill-switch + override steps - Postmortem template with prefilled sections for fast RCA Links & artifacts: - Draft runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ops/Canary+Regression+Sleuth+Runbook - Incident ticket we are addressing: https://linear.redwood.ai/ENG-42109 - Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1482 - Sleuth console mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1AbCdEfG - Canary telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/canary/regression-hunter-dashboard
comments: 2025-02-19 - Ava Chen: Kickoff sync with Reliability and Console teams. Agreed to two-signal default for safety; Reliability will own latency signal extraction, Console will scope UI controls.
2025-02-22 - Liam Patel: PoC detector ingests canary metrics. Initial false positive rate ~12% on historical backtesting; tuned thresholds to reduce to ~4% with negligible detection latency increase.
2025-02-25 - Sophie Ng (review): Requested clearer audit log schema and opt-in defaults for enterprise orgs. Added requirement to redact PII from captured samples.
2025-02-27 - David Ortiz: Prototype quarantine action wired to traffic router (test cluster only). Verified routing flipback works in 45s in lab.

2025-03-03 - QA: Began shadow experiments on internal beta routes; detector fired 3 times, two were true regressions validated by manual eval; one was noisy infra blip and will inform threshold changes.
2025-03-05 - Liam Patel: Branch created for phase 2 (serving:feature/sleuth-policy). Next: add ticket creation integration and postmortem template automation.
next_steps: 1) Complete phase 1 PoC and record backtest metrics (false positive/negative rates) by 2025-03-07. 2) Implement audit log schema and KMS-safe storage by 2025-03-10. 3) Ship phase 2 gating and ticket automation before enabling opt-in testing on early access tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Detector raises standardized event within 30s for sustained deviations in lab backtests
Quarantine action can redirect affected slice and revert to stable variant within 60s in test cluster
Auto-postmortem ticket is populated with samples and links automatically when quarantine triggers in non-shadow mode
Two-signal default prevents automated quarantine for single noisy infra signals in 95% of historical cases
